NDT training in Seattle: how it works for Seattle employers and technicians

Atlantis NDT delivers ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based NDT training for Seattle and the Puget Sound region at Level I, II and III in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET. Theory is taught live online and practical training runs onsite at your facility under ASNT Level III oversight. Certification is granted by your employer under its written practice after classroom hours, documented experience, general, specific and practical exams and a vision test.

Seattle has one of the densest concentrations of inspection work on the West Coast, but it is spread across very different industries: aircraft production and its supply chain, naval and commercial ship repair, refineries in Skagit and Whatcom counties and in Tacoma, port cranes, hydroelectric and transmission assets, and a steady stream of bridge, transit and building construction. A technician who understands that spread can plan a far better career route than one who simply looks for the nearest class. An employer who understands it can build a training plan that satisfies its own customers instead of buying generic courses.

Two things are worth being clear about from the start. First, Atlantis has no physical training centre in Seattle, Everett, Tacoma or anywhere else. We teach the formal classroom content live online, in real time with an instructor, and we deliver the hands-on training and practical examinations onsite at the employer's facility, using the employer's equipment and representative specimens. Second, under SNT-TC-1A the certificate is issued by the employer, not by a training provider or by ASNT. A course completion record is evidence of training hours; certification also depends on experience, examinations and the employer's written practice.

The Seattle enquiries we see most often come from supplier shops that have been asked by an aerospace customer to formalise their penetrant, magnetic particle or eddy current function; from marine and industrial maintenance contractors that need Level II UT and MT to satisfy a client; from refinery and terminal contractors preparing crews for turnaround season; from individuals moving into NDT from aircraft maintenance, machining, welding or the military; and from senior Level IIs preparing for the ASNT Level III examinations. The sections that follow are organised so each of those readers can find the part that applies.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses available in Seattle

All eight methods are available to Seattle employers and technicians. Level I and Level II method courses are delivered live online for theory with onsite practical training; Level III preparation is delivered live online. The third column shows how the method is typically used in the Puget Sound economy, as context rather than a guarantee of which methods any single employer needs.

MethodLevelsWhat Seattle employers use it forPrerequisite
Ultrasonic testing (UT)I, II, III prepComposite laminate and bond inspection in aerospace supply, weld examination in ship repair and structural steel, thickness surveys in refineries and terminalsNone for Level I; Level I plus documented experience for Level II
Phased array UT (PAUT)II, III prepWeld examination in heavy fabrication and refinery piping, corrosion mapping, and composite inspection in aerospaceConventional UT Level II recommended
Time-of-flight diffraction (TOFD)II, III prepFlaw sizing in thick pressure-vessel and heavy-structure welds, often paired with PAUT during turnaroundsConventional UT Level II recommended
Radiographic testing (RT)I, II, III prepPipe welds in refineries and pipelines, castings, ship systems and fabrication-shop pressure workNone for Level I; radiation-safety certification is a separate regulatory requirement
Magnetic particle testing (MT)I, II, III prepFerrous aerospace parts, ship structure, crane and bridge welds, rail and heavy equipmentNone for Level I
Liquid penetrant testing (PT)I, II, III prepAluminium and titanium aerospace details, stainless piping, machined and cast componentsNone for Level I
Visual testing (VT)I, II, III prepWeld and structural visual inspection across construction, marine and plant workNone for Level I
Eddy current testing (ET)I, II, III prepFastener holes, surface cracks and conductivity on aircraft structure, heat-exchanger tubing in refineriesNone for Level I; PT or MT background helps

Choosing a first method in Puget Sound. Seattle is one of the few US markets where eddy current and penetrant are as central as magnetic particle and UT, because so much local work involves aluminium, titanium and composite aircraft structure. For a newcomer aiming at the aerospace supply chain, PT and ET are sensible early methods, followed by UT, which is increasingly important as composite content grows. For someone aiming at ship repair, refinery or construction work, VT and MT are the usual entry points, with UT as the method that most often leads to a Level II role that can sign off volumetric weld examination. PAUT and TOFD should come after conventional UT; employers performing turnaround work in the refineries north and south of Seattle increasingly specify them for weld and corrosion work.

Every Atlantis method course covers principles and physics, equipment and materials, calibration and reference standards, technique selection, detection and characterisation of indications, application of acceptance criteria, and documentation. Level II adds setting up techniques from written procedures, evaluating results against codes and specifications, and guiding Level I personnel. For Level III preparation, see the ASNT Level III training page; for the method list and levels, see NDT training.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Seattle, step by step

This is the standard SNT-TC-1A sequence. Your employer's written practice fills in the details, and it can require more than the recommended minimums. The recommended training and experience hours by method and level are in our training requirements matrix.

  1. Identify the written practice that will govern you. A Tier 2 aerospace supplier in Kent, a ship-repair contractor in Bremerton and a refinery contractor in Anacortes can all be SNT-TC-1A employers with quite different written practices and customer overlays.
  2. Complete formal training. Attend method-specific classroom training for the target level. Keep the course outline, hours and instructor records.
  3. Accumulate documented experience. Work in the method under certified supervision and log it as you go: dates, techniques, parts or systems, and hours, verified by your supervisor.
  4. General examination. A written test on method principles, prepared and graded under the authority of a Level III.
  5. Specific examination. A written test on your employer's equipment, procedures, specifications and acceptance criteria.
  6. Practical examination. Demonstrate the technique on real specimens: set-up, calibration, detection, evaluation and reporting, administered under the written practice.
  7. Vision examination. Near-vision acuity and colour-contrast differentiation, with near vision re-checked at least annually.
  8. Employer certification. The employer certifies you in writing for the method and level. The certification stays with that employer.
  9. Maintain and recertify. Keep vision current, maintain continuity in the method, and recertify at the interval in your written practice. A new employer certifies you under its own written practice, and may credit your documented training and experience.

More detail on each step, and on what auditors expect in personnel files, is on our SNT-TC-1A training and certification page.

Online, live-virtual or onsite NDT training for Seattle crews

Live online theory. Classroom content is taught in real time by an instructor, not as a self-paced video library. For Seattle crews this removes commuting across the region, which matters when a trainee lives in Marysville and works in Renton, or when a crew is split between Everett, Tacoma and a job site in Anacortes. Sessions can be scheduled in blocks that fit around shift patterns. Details are on the online NDT training page.

Onsite practical at your facility. Hands-on training and practical examinations are delivered at the employer's site, anywhere in the Puget Sound area, using your equipment, your reference standards and specimens representative of your work. For an aerospace supplier, that can mean practising on the part families the customer actually buys; for a marine contractor, on the plate and pipe configurations found in ship repair; for a refinery contractor, on corroded pipe and weld samples like those examined in a turnaround.

Scheduling around local calendars. Refinery turnarounds in Anacortes, Ferndale, Cherry Point and Tacoma draw heavily on the regional inspection workforce, and naval and commercial yard availabilities create similar peaks. Aerospace suppliers are driven by production rates. The sensible approach is to complete theory during quieter periods and run the onsite practical so trainees are examined and certified before the next turnaround or yard period, not during it. We build that timetable with you. Onsite and cohort quotes are returned within one business day, and multi-site or recurring programmes can be organised through our corporate NDT training service. Ask about onsite training for your Seattle crew.

Where NDT technicians work in Seattle

Aerospace manufacturing and the supply chain. Commercial aircraft final assembly in Everett and Renton, composite and fabrication sites in Auburn and Frederickson, and hundreds of suppliers across King, Snohomish and Pierce counties generate constant demand for PT, ET, UT (including composite UT) and MT. Space-industry manufacturers in Kent and Redmond add further demand for precision inspection. Aerospace customers typically require their own process specifications, and many require NAS 410 or EN 4179 qualification and Nadcap-accredited processes. Atlantis training is SNT-TC-1A-based and does not provide NAS 410 certification; aerospace employers can use our method training and Level III support as part of their own qualification scheme, but should confirm what their customer requires.

Naval and commercial ship repair. Puget Sound Naval Shipyard and Intermediate Maintenance Facility in Bremerton, Naval Station Everett, and commercial yards on Harbor Island and in the Duwamish Waterway maintain naval vessels, ferries, fishing fleets and tugs. Naval work is governed by NAVSEA requirements such as Technical Publication T9074-AS-GIB-010/271 for NDT, alongside MIL-STD weld and inspection standards, which bring their own qualification rules. Commercial ship repair uses classification-society and ABS rules. VT, MT, PT, UT and RT are all heavily used.

Refining and fuel terminals. Refineries in Anacortes, Ferndale and near Blaine at Cherry Point, and the refinery and terminals on the Tacoma tideflats, run inspection programmes under ASME B31.3 for process piping and ASME Section VIII for pressure vessels, with in-service inspection following API codes. UT thickness and weld work, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT and ET of heat-exchanger tubing are all routine, and turnaround seasons are when demand peaks. Some refinery owners also require API 510, 570 or 653 inspectors on the owner's side; those certifications are separate and not offered by Atlantis.

Ports, cranes and rail. The Northwest Seaport Alliance terminals in Seattle and Tacoma, BNSF and Union Pacific rail yards and the heavy-equipment businesses around them rely on MT and UT of crane structures, wheels, axles and lifting equipment, commonly following AWS D1.1 and D14.1 for structural and crane welding.

Bridges, transit and construction. WSDOT's steel and floating bridges, Sound Transit light-rail expansion and major building construction put VT, MT and UT to work on structural welds, with bridge steel typically welded and inspected under AWS D1.5. Construction inspection firms supporting these projects often need Level II UT technicians for full-penetration welds.

Power and utilities. Hydroelectric dams in the Skagit and Cascade systems and further east on the Columbia, transmission structures and gas utility pipelines generate penstock, turbine, structural and pipeline weld inspection. Pipeline welding in Washington commonly follows API 1104. The Hanford Site near Richland is a separate market with its own quality-assurance requirements.

Radiography licensing in Washington. Washington is an NRC Agreement State. Industrial radiography with radioactive sources is licensed by the Washington State Department of Health, Office of Radiation Protection, under state rules compatible with federal 10 CFR Part 34, and the department also regulates X-ray equipment. Radiographers must meet state training and certification requirements for radiation safety, commonly shown through a recognised radiographer certification such as ASNT IRRSP. Work on federal sites or across the border in British Columbia follows other rules. Our RT course covers the NDT method and film or digital interpretation; it is not a substitute for the radiation-safety training and certification your licence demands.

A note for crews working in British Columbia. In Canada the national scheme is CAN/CGSB-48.9712, based on ISO 9712. Atlantis training is SNT-TC-1A-based and suits employers working to US codes and US clients; it is not CGSB certification, and we do not claim CGSB recognition.

Seattle-area employers generally look for a current Level II in the relevant method, verifiable experience logs, a current vision record and, for aerospace and naval work, familiarity with working to a customer specification. For pay information we point to our NDT salary guide rather than quoting local figures we cannot verify.

Level III services and written practices for Seattle NDT companies

The Puget Sound supply chain is full of companies that perform inspection as one part of a wider business: machine shops finishing aerospace parts, composite fabricators, marine contractors, crane and rigging firms, structural fabricators and mechanical contractors. When a customer audit asks "show me your written practice and your Level III", these companies often discover that their inspection function has grown faster than its paperwork.

Atlantis helps in three ways. Written-practice development: we write or revise a written practice that fits your methods, levels, customer overlays and organisation, and that people can actually follow. Level III services: preparing and administering examinations, writing and reviewing procedures and technique sheets, and reviewing certification files so they will stand up to a customer or third-party audit. Integrated training plans: method training scheduled so that classroom hours, experience logs and examinations are recorded in a consistent way from day one. The employer's obligations under the recommended practice are explained on our SNT-TC-1A guidance page.

For a supplier facing its first audit, the order we recommend is: update or create the written practice; list who needs which method and level; gap-analyse existing training and experience records; then train and examine. It prevents training people under rules that will change a month later. Book a Level III consultation for your Seattle company.

Practise before the practical exam

Hands-on confidence is often the weakest point for candidates who study well but have had limited time on equipment. Atlantis trainees have access to the Practical NDT 3D simulator, which lets them practise 12 NDT methods in five environments: an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank. For Seattle technicians the aircraft hangar and oil and gas environments line up well with the region's two biggest inspection markets.

The simulator is a practice aid only. It helps trainees rehearse set-ups, scanning and indication recognition between sessions, but it does not replace the practical examination on real specimens required by your written practice, and simulator time is not on-the-job experience. For written-exam revision, use our UT Level 2 practice questions and the similar mock-exam articles on the blog.

Your instructor

Training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. He is responsible for course content, examination preparation and the Level III side of each programme, including written-practice and procedure work for employers. Seattle trainees learn from the same instructional team and materials used across all Atlantis programmes, delivered live online and onsite at the employer's facility.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Seattle

How do I get NDT certified in Seattle?

Under ASNT SNT-TC-1A, your employer certifies you after you complete formal method training, build documented experience under supervision, pass general, specific and practical examinations administered under a Level III, and pass a vision test. Atlantis delivers the training and exam preparation and, for employers, the written practice and Level III services.

Can I take NDT training online in Washington State?

Yes, the theory portion of every Atlantis method course is delivered live online, so trainees across Washington can attend. The practical training and practical examination must be completed hands-on with real equipment and specimens, which we run onsite at the employer's facility.

Does Atlantis have a training centre in Seattle?

No. Atlantis does not operate a physical training centre in Seattle. Training is delivered live online and onsite at your company's facility under ASNT Level III oversight.

How long does UT Level 2 training take?

It depends on your employer's written practice and what you already hold. SNT-TC-1A recommends minimum classroom and experience hours for Level I and Level II, and the experience requirement usually takes longer than the classroom portion. Check the training requirements matrix for the recommended figures.

Do I need a license for radiography in Washington?

Companies performing industrial radiography with radioactive material need a licence from the Washington State Department of Health, Office of Radiation Protection, because Washington is an Agreement State. Individual radiographers must meet the state's radiation-safety training and certification requirements. Your RT method certification under SNT-TC-1A is a separate requirement.

What does NDT training cost in Seattle?

We do not publish prices. The cost depends on method, level, group size, onsite delivery and whether Level III or written-practice work is included. Cohort and onsite quotes are returned within one business day. Request a Seattle training quote.

Is ASNT certification recognised by Seattle employers?

SNT-TC-1A is the most widely used US framework, and many Seattle-area fabrication, marine, refinery and construction employers work within it. Aerospace primes and naval programmes often add their own requirements, such as NAS 410 or NAVSEA rules, which Atlantis does not certify to. SNT-TC-1A certification is employer-based, so a new employer recertifies you under its own written practice.

Which NDT method is most in demand around Seattle?

It depends on sector. Aerospace suppliers lean heavily on PT, ET and UT; ship repair, cranes and construction on VT, MT and UT; refineries on UT, PAUT, RT and ET. Ask your current or target employer which methods its written practice and customers need before you choose.

Can our company certify its own inspectors?

Yes. Under SNT-TC-1A the employer certifies its own personnel. You need a written practice, a Level III to administer or oversee examinations, and complete training and experience records. Atlantis can supply all three.

Is Atlantis training valid in British Columbia?

Atlantis training is SNT-TC-1A-based. Canada's national scheme is CAN/CGSB-48.9712 (ISO 9712), and our training is not CGSB certification. It suits employers working to US codes and US clients.

Do you offer ASNT Level III exam preparation for Seattle candidates?

Yes. Live-online Level III preparation covers the Basic examination and method examinations. See ASNT Level III training.

Do you offer NAS 410, API or CWI training?

No. Atlantis offers ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based training only. Some Seattle employers also ask for NAS 410, API inspector certifications or AWS CWI, which are obtained through their own schemes. Our method training complements them but does not replace them.
